title: Selling one option naked
summary: A single sold call or put with no bought leg: more premium, an open-ended loss, more margin, and the stop-loss as your only floor.

questions.q: Compared with a spread, a naked sold put:
options: Has no floor under the loss
questions.why: Without a bought put, the loss grows the further the stock falls.

questions.q: Why is the margin for a naked sale larger?
options: The exchange blocks for a big move, not a capped one
questions.why: Margin follows the worst case, which is much larger without a floor.

questions.q: With a naked sale, what limits the loss in practice?
questions.why: With no bought leg, the stop-loss is the only floor.

questions.q: A single naked sale would block half your account's capital. You should:
questions.why: One bad move shouldn't be able to decide your month.

questions.q: When do you unlock selling both sides naked (the short strangle)?
questions.why: The strangle comes at Level 5, after months of discipline.
